components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      x-class-extra-annotation: "@org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.PostcodeValidation @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.AddressValidation"
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The optional honorific title of the pet owner. When present it is
            one of 'MR', 'MRS', 'MS' or 'DR' and is used to compose the
            read-only 'salutation'.
          type: string
          enum:
            - MR
            - MRS

## Summary

I implemented idempotent owner creation keyed on the `Idempotency-Key` request header, following the project's contract-first Spring conventions.

**1. `src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added the `Idempotency-Key` optional header parameter to the `addOwner` operation, plus a `200` response describing the idempotent-replay case. The OpenAPI generator then produces the interface method `addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto, String idempotencyKey)` with a `@RequestHeader(value = "Idempotency-Key", required = false)` binding — the idiomatic way this codebase surfaces request inputs.

**2. `src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`**
- Added an in-memory `idempotencyKeys` map (`ConcurrentHashMap<String, Integer>`) mapping a seen key → the created owner's id.
- Updated `addOwner` to the new signature. At the start, if the key was already seen and its owner still exists, it returns that original owner with **200 OK** — skipping the create and its duplicate/quota rejections. After a successful `saveOwner`, it records the key → new owner id.
- Extracted the read-path DTO assembly (setting the derived `householdSize` and `bulkSignupWarning` fields) into a shared `toOwnerDtoWithDerived` helper, reused by both `getOwner` and the idempotent replay so the replayed body matches a normal read.

The acceptance test `coreIdempotentRepeat` confirms a repeat with the same key returns 200 with the same id instead of a 409 duplicate.

A note on durability: the key store is in-memory and per-instance, which satisfies the spec and tests here but wouldn't survive a restart or work across multiple app instances. If you want cross-instance/persistent idempotency later, that'd move to a database table or shared cache — happy to do that if it's in scope.
